counterfactual_missing_items: lobulated mass in cutis and subcutis
decisive_items: marked vascularity of the mass, supplied by branches of the left superficial temporal and posterior auricular arteries
irregular, friable surface and bleeding on minimal contact
response.rationale: R5 is the strongest because it directly matches the marked vascularity and friable bleeding, which are hallmarks of angiosarcoma. R4 relies on generic atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation, which are less specific. The provisional diagnosis of a malignant tumor without subtype is consistent with angiosarcoma.

rejected.why: Only one raw span (atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation) is too generic and does not support a rare granular cell tumor.
Lacks vascularity and friable bleeding; Merkel cell carcinoma is not typical for the ear canal and has no specific supporting evidence.
Infection is contradicted by the provisional diagnosis of a malignant tumor.
Langerhans cell histiocytosis is not a malignant tumor and lacks the vascularity evidence.
